chunk-001:c004.proposition: Causal finitism is unnecessary because the unsatisfiable-pair diagnosis blocks the paradox by rejecting only the contradictory combination.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive move, the same proposition supplies a standalone alternative diagnosis: reject the jointly contradictory conditions without rejecting every infinite causal history.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Because both diagnoses exclude the paradox equally well, parsimony favors the logically minimal unsatisfiable-pair account over causal finitism.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently compares the commitments of the two diagnoses and gives parsimony as an affirmative reason to prefer the logically minimal account.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Ordinary rearrangement can cross from possibility into logical impossibility, so recombination intuitions do not by themselves preserve possibility.

orphanFallback.rationale: The bridge-rearrangement counterexample independently establishes that manipulable components need not remain jointly possible after rearrangement, limiting recombination as a modal principle.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Infinite recombination is epistemically unreliable, normally caveated, and cannot transfer the impossibility of a joint configuration to either component alone.

orphanFallback.rationale: Taken constructively, the proposition states a general modal limitation: an impossible conjunction does not show that either ingredient is impossible, especially under disputed infinite recombination.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Apparently unnecessary suffering is more expected under indifference than under perfect theism and therefore provides modest evidence favoring indifference.

orphanFallback.rationale: This is already a standalone likelihood argument comparing the expectation of apparently unnecessary suffering under indifference and perfect theism.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: No quantity of compensating benefit automatically makes deliberately causing or permitting atrocities morally acceptable, because some harms resist an aggregative ledger of goods and evils.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently advances a nonaggregative moral constraint on greater-good theodicies: compensating benefits alone do not automatically justify permitting atrocities.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Shared moral knowledge in clear cases permits judging that permitting torture is wrong regardless of compensating goods, and many actual sufferings appear relevantly similar to those cases.

orphanFallback.rationale: As a constructive argument, the proposition grounds limits on moral skepticism in shared judgments about clear torture cases and their similarity to actual suffering.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-09.proposition: A theism compatible with every possible observation becomes unfalsifiable and cannot connect worldly events strongly enough to rationally affect belief.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition stands alone as an epistemic-discipline argument: a hypothesis insulated from every possible observation loses meaningful confirmatory and disconfirmatory contact with worldly evidence.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-01.proposition: A world that requires some people to endure extreme deprivation for others' flourishing would distribute suffering unfairly and callously.

orphanFallback.rationale: Constructively read, the proposition identifies unequal allocation as an independent moral defect in any world-level justification that makes some people's extreme deprivation serve others' flourishing.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-04.proposition: Although consciousness in the abstract may initially appear more likely on theism, its precarious dependence on alterable brain matter fits an accidental natural process better than deliberate divine production.

orphanFallback.rationale: The proposition independently demonstrates why comparative likelihoods must use fine-grained evidence: consciousness's observed physical precariousness may favor accident despite its coarse-grained existence favoring theism.
